label: vesicular
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing small, bladder-like, thin-walled cells or outgrowths filled with fluid or air. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991059 papillose; not PATO:0001928 blistered, which is damage, nor PATO:0002376 inflated, which applies to the whole structure.
reason: Seeds, fruits and perianth bearing bladder-like cells or hairs (as in Chenopodiaceae and Aizoaceae); no PATO or FLOPO class covers this.

label: semicordate
definition: A heart shaped quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like one half of a heart, the base being cordate on one side of the midline only.
reason: Common for unequal-sided leaflets, stipules and wing bases; PATO heart shaped is the symmetrical whole shape.

label: catenulate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of leaves by virtue of their being closely imbricate and individually incurved, so that the shoot looks like a chain of links. NOTE: Bryological usage, mostly of dry leaves; sibling of FLOPO:0991063 imbricate.
reason: A moss leaf-arrangement term (FNA bryophytes, often 'when dry'); the French 'disposées en chaînette' has the same sense. The meaning outside mosses is less certain.
untwisted = not twisted: negation of PATO torsioned (EXACT synonym twisted).
A count of flowers (many, as opposed to uniflorous) in one word, like 'few-flowered'; it belongs in the count pattern, not in a quality term.

Sheaths, blades and calyces that do not break up into parts = not split. On fruits and capsules the better reading is not dehiscent (negation of FLOPO:0991149 dehiscent), and the rule should map to that for those bearers.

cirrose = ending in or drawn out into a slender coiling tendril-like tip: PATO tendrilous (slender and spirally coiled; RELATED synonym tendril-like). Tendrils made from leaf apices could instead be leaf apex tendril (PO_0025363) present.
caudiculate = pollinia bearing caudicles; the FLOPO caudicle class exists. 'sepal: caudiculées' is a transcription that attached the word to the wrong part.

label: polygamodioecious
definition: A polygamous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing flowers of one sex together with some bisexual flowers, so that the species is functionally dioecious. NOTE: Child of FLOPO:0991177 polygamous; with FLOPO:0991072 dioecious.
reason: A standard breeding-system term that is more specific than polygamous; it follows the earlier monoecious, dioecious and andromonoecious classes.

target: lobed (PATO_0001979) negated, on plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024)
reason: The base of the part is not lobed: the region rule puts the bearer at the base, and the quality is the negation of PATO lobed. 'basal lobe' was rejected earlier as a generic part.

label: polystichous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being arranged in many longitudinal rows round the axis that bears it. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0001952 distichous (two rows).
reason: Leaves, bracts and flowers in many ranks; PATO has distichous only. 'polystichously 8-15-flowered' also carries a count, which goes in the count pattern.

label: intravaginal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a shoot by virtue of its growing upward inside the sheath of the leaf that subtends it, without breaking through the sheath. NOTE: Botany-specific (grasses, sedges); opposite of extravaginal.
reason: A standard character of grass and sedge innovations with no PATO or FLOPO term.
A stylopodium or operculum shaped like a cone; 'low' is a relative proportion that has no term, so the shape is annotated as conical.
A compound of two shape values (like 'linear-lanceolate'); this is the continuum pattern, not a new term.
Mostly 'with a collar': a ring-like part whose meaning changes with the organ (chalazal collar, stigma rim, achene apex). It needs the organ it belongs to, like 'ring' and 'rim' before.

label: ternate
definition: A split quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being divided into three parts, each of which may itself be divided again in threes. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991160 pedate; FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate is a leaf of exactly three leaflets.
reason: Leaf blades divided in threes, often repeatedly; trifoliolate does not cover repeated division. '2-3 × ternately divided' adds a count, which goes in the count pattern.
sub- = nearly, as in 'suborbicular': tomentose with the 'approximately' qualifier.
vinaceous = the colour of red wine, a purplish red; PATO reddish purple is the closest colour class. 'vinaccous' is a misspelling.

target: new: coloured marking (streaked FLOPO:0991206 on the bearer + purple PATO_0000951 on the streaks)
reason: A compound of a marking value and the colour of the marks; making a term for each colour would multiply terms.
Rachillas and stem segments that do not break apart at their joints = not jointed in the FLOPO sense (having joints at which it readily separates).
corneous = horny: hard and resistant, as with endocarps, arils and tooth tips. PATO hard, as for 'indurate'; FLOPO cartilaginous (sensu botany) is the tougher, more flexible texture.
A margin cut irregularly = FLOPO lacerate. PATO cut (EXACT synonym incised) is defined as regularly divided, so it does not fit.
A compound of two shape values; this is the continuum pattern.

target: new: size gradient along a series
reason: Leaves, scales or lobes getting smaller along a series ('decrescent upwards'): a comparison between members of a series, not a quality of any one of them.
aseptate = without septa: the complement of has_part some septum.
tabular = flat like a table (flat papillae and appendages, plank-like roots and wings, a flat-topped crown). 'racines tabulaires' could also be mapped to FLOPO:0991138 buttressed on the trunk.
multistratose = more than one cell layer thick (moss leaves and margins): PATO stratified, a layered configuration.
rugulate = finely rugose: PATO rugose (broader), as with lobulate → lobed.
A triangle longer than broad; the proportion has no term. PATO isosceles triangular does not say the shape is elongated.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: margin + purple PATO_0000951)
reason: The margin of the part is purple: the region pattern makes the margin the bearer (e.g. leaf margin PO_0020128) and gives it the colour.
